title: Add momentum/breakout strategy layer to capture missed trending signals
analysis: The journal shows a structural signal leak of significant scale. On 2026-05-22, AAPL fired 'RSI>65, AboveMA20>1%, ADX>25 (trending)' and was rejected 5 consecutive times solely because the bot already held 33 shares — not because the signal was wrong. The same pattern occurred with AMD on 2026-05-20 (executed at $443.67, signal score 4, R:R 2.0) and META on 2026-05-19 (4 rejections with score 4, R:R 3.1-3.36). Critically, these are NOT mean reversion signals — they are momentum signals: RSI>65, AboveMA20>1%, ADX>25. The bot's signal scoring engine is already generating valid momentum readings, but the strategy identity (mean reversion only) causes them to be wasted or, worse in the AMD case, executed anyway without a proper momentum framework around them. The macro context supports this: SPY at $745.64 is $14.06 (1.92%) above its 20-day MA of $731.58, Technology sector is +3.46% over 5 days, Healthcare +2.86%, and VIX at 16.7 indicates a risk-on, trending environment — not a ranging one. ADX>25 on multiple instruments confirms the market is in a trending regime where mean reversion carries structural headwinds.
rationale: The bot is operating a mean reversion strategy in a regime that its own ADX filter identifies as trending (ADX>25). Rule 6 correctly blocks mean reversion entries when ADX>30, but leaves a dead zone between ADX 25-30 and provides no alternative. The result is opportunity cost: valid momentum entries are generated, partially executed (AMD), mostly rejected, and never systematically captured. Adding a parallel momentum/breakout layer with its own position sizing, entry criteria (RSI>60 + ADX>25 + price above 20-day MA + volume confirmation), and separate position slots would allow the system to profit from the current regime without dismantling the mean reversion core for when ranging returns.

insight.why_now: Technology is +3.46% in 5 days, SPY is 1.92% above its MA20, multiple watchlist symbols (AAPL, AMD) are printing momentum signals on consecutive cycles, and VIX at 16.7 sits in a low-fear trending environment. The bot already detected these signals — it just has no framework to act on them systematically.
insight.purpose: Create a second strategy module that activates when ADX>25 and captures momentum continuation trades that the current system structurally ignores, converting rejected signals into P&L.
insight.expected_effect: On the observed data, 5 AAPL rejections and 4 META rejections occurred over 3 days with R:R of 2.0-3.36. Capturing even 40% of these would materially improve weekly P&L. More importantly, it aligns capital deployment with prevailing market regime rather than fighting it.
insight.risks: Regime transitions are the most dangerous period — if trend reverses sharply, a momentum position initiated near the top suffers maximum drawdown. Requires strict ATR-based stops and must not share position slots with mean reversion trades to avoid correlated exposure doubling.

current_rule: 6. TREND FILTER: If ADX > 30, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals.
proposed_rule: 6. TREND FILTER: If ADX > 30, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals. MOMENTUM MODULE (parallel): If ADX > 25 AND RSI > 60 AND price > MA20 by >1% AND volume > 20-day avg volume, evaluate momentum entry under MOMENTUM RULES (separate position slots, max 2 momentum positions, 1% risk per trade, ATR trailing stop 1.0x, target = entry + 2x ATR). Mean reversion and momentum positions count toward the shared 5-position max.

title: AAPL and AMD are structurally poor mean reversion candidates — replace or reclassify
analysis: AAPL generated 7 momentum signals (RSI>65, AboveMA20>1%, ADX>25) across 2026-05-20 and 2026-05-22 with zero mean reversion signals. AMD on 2026-05-20 was bought on a momentum signal (RSI>65, ADX>25, PositiveSentiment) at $443.67 with a $49.68 target move — this is a breakout trade, not mean reversion. META on 2026-05-19 showed mild mean reversion signals (RSI<45, BelowMA20>1%) with R:R of 3.1-3.36, suggesting it has some mean reversion validity. AAPL and AMD are high-momentum, high-ADX instruments in the current environment. Per market regime theory, strongly directional stocks are structurally poor mean reversion candidates — their mean is moving, making reversion to a fixed MA20 an unreliable target. QQQ (bought 2026-05-22 at $721.55 on a breakout signal) is a better fit for mean reversion due to its diversified ETF nature, though the entry itself was a breakout. The watchlist appears to be shared between strategy types without differentiation.
rationale: Running mean reversion logic on momentum stocks like AAPL and AMD wastes scan cycles, generates noise signals that confuse the regime filter, and risks entering counter-trend positions on instruments with strong directional bias. Segregating the watchlist into mean-reversion-suitable (ETFs: SPY, QQQ, GLD; range-bound sector ETFs: XLV, XLP) and momentum-suitable (AAPL, AMD, NVDA, sector leaders) would improve signal quality and reduce rejected-trade volume.

insight.why_now: Over the observed 50-entry window, AAPL produced 7 signals and 0 valid mean reversion entries. AMD produced 1 momentum entry. The watchlist is generating high noise-to-signal ratio on these names in the current trending regime.
insight.purpose: Improve signal purity by ensuring mean reversion scans only run on instruments with demonstrated range-bound behavior (low average ADX, high historical BB touch rate), and routing momentum stocks to the momentum module if one is added.
insight.expected_effect: Fewer REJECTED entries, cleaner journal, reduced computational waste, and better-fit trades when mean reversion conditions do appear. Eliminates the structural ambiguity of the AMD buy (momentum signals executed by a mean reversion bot).
insight.risks: Watchlist segregation requires backtesting to confirm which instruments have historically shown mean reversion properties. Misclassification could remove a genuinely range-bound instrument from the MR scan.

proposed_rule: WATCHLIST SEGMENTATION: Mean reversion scans run only on instruments with 90-day average ADX < 22 and at least 3 Bollinger Band touches per month historically (preferred: SPY, QQQ, GLD, XLV, XLP, sector ETFs). High-ADX momentum instruments (AAPL, AMD, NVDA and any symbol where 30-day ADX > 25) are excluded from mean reversion scans and routed to momentum module only. Review segmentation monthly.

title: Anomalous SKIP entries with HIGH confidence signal a decision-engine parsing failure
analysis: The journal contains a recurring pattern of entries where confidence='HIGH', signal_score=0, signals_fired=[], action='SKIP', and stop_loss/entry_price are null. These appear on: 2026-05-19 16:12 (confidence HIGH, score 0), 2026-05-20 14:39 (confidence HIGH, score 0, symbol='NONE'), 2026-05-21 at 12:26, 12:41, 13:32, 13:42, 13:49, 14:19 — all confidence HIGH with zero signals. This is internally contradictory: a system with zero signals firing should output LOW confidence, not HIGH. This pattern suggests the LLM decision engine is outputting HIGH confidence on SKIP decisions (possibly expressing confidence in the skip itself) rather than confidence in a trade signal. However, this creates a data integrity problem — the confidence field becomes uninterpretable in the journal and weekly review process. Additionally, on 2026-05-21, 12 of 12 entries were SKIP with 4 open positions held all day — the system appears to have been in a passive hold state all day but continued cycling without useful output. The AMD entry on 2026-05-20 executed momentum signals through a mean reversion framework without the journal flagging strategy mismatch, suggesting no guardrail catches cross-strategy signal contamination.
rationale: Behavioral integrity of journal data is critical for the weekly review process. If confidence='HIGH' appears on SKIP entries, the weekly review prompt ('identify win rate and average R-multiple') will produce corrupted statistics. The anomalous HIGH-confidence SKIPs also mask whether the system genuinely had no signals or was failing to parse market data correctly. A rule requiring confidence to reflect trade signal strength (and default to 'N/A' or be omitted on SKIP entries) would restore journal data integrity and make the weekly review actionable.

insight.why_now: On 2026-05-21, 8+ consecutive HIGH-confidence SKIP entries occurred while 4 positions were open and the day was oscillating between +$98 and -$284. The confidence field is clearly being misused as 'confidence in the skip decision' rather than 'confidence in a trade signal.' This corrupts performance analytics.
insight.purpose: Restore semantic integrity to the confidence field so weekly review statistics (win rate by confidence tier, signal quality analysis) are meaningful and actionable.
insight.expected_effect: Cleaner weekly review data, ability to filter trades by genuine signal confidence, and early detection of decision-engine malfunction when SKIPs cluster with inconsistent metadata.
insight.risks: Low risk. This is a logging/output format fix. The main risk is that enforcing the rule requires the LLM to self-monitor its output schema, which may produce occasional non-compliance without automated validation.

proposed_rule: "confidence": "HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW|N/A" — RULE: confidence field reflects strength of trade signal ONLY. If action is SKIP or HOLD with no active trade signal, confidence MUST be 'N/A'. HIGH = 4+ signals aligned with strong RSI reading. MEDIUM = 2-3 signals. LOW = minimum threshold met. Never assign HIGH confidence to a zero-signal SKIP.
